text:
ashley: Heads-up — saw a burst of Xid errors on prod-us-east last night. Thought we should standardize a tiny "triage sampler" that runs on-demand (or via infra-bot) to collect dmesg/journalctl/nvidia-smi snapshots and upload them for quick root-cause. Anyone already have a compact script/playbook?

matt: We have ad-hoc scripts in eng-scripts but not something uniform. Agree on standardized collector. Minimal requirements: timestamped archive, GPU UUID, ECC counts, kernel oops + recent logs, and metadata (node, pod list). Prefer S3 upload with short TTL.

sofia: +1. Quick collector I use during manual triage (can be systemd oneshot or run in container):
```bash
TS=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
HOST=$(hostname -s)
OUT=/tmp/gpu-triage/${HOST}-${TS}
mkdir -p "$OUT"
dmesg -T | tail -n 800 > "$OUT/dmesg.txt"
journalctl -k -b -0 --no-pager > "$OUT/journal-k.txt"
journalctl -u kubelet --since "2 hours ago" --no-pager > "$OUT/journal-kubelet.txt"
nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,DIAG,PERF > "$OUT/nvidia-smi.txt"
cat /var/log/syslog | tail -n 500 > "$OUT/syslog.tail" || true
# collect GPU process list
nvidia-smi pmon -c 1 > "$OUT/nvidia-pmon.txt"
tar czf "/tmp/${HOST}-${TS}.tgz" -C /tmp "gpu-triage/${HOST}-${TS}"
aws s3 cp "/tmp/${HOST}-${TS}.tgz" s3://redwood-gpu-triage/ --acl private --storage-class STANDARD_IA
```

ryan: Nice. A couple notes:
- Capture `dmesg | grep -i xid` separately so triagers see Xid lines first.
- For journalctl include `-o short-iso` so timestamps are consistent.
- If we run via daemon, make sure to rotate local /tmp to avoid filling disk.

kyle: We should also capture container context for any GPU holders: `crictl ps --format json` or `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=$HOST` and include the pod yaml for suspicious containers.

ashley: Agreed. Thinking infra-bot can run the collector automatically when we detect Xid spike or ECC increase. infra-bot: can you post a sample alert payload we can hook to the collector?

infra-bot: Alert: 3 Xid 31 errors observed on gpu-prod-052 at 2026-03-15T21:13:02Z. Suggested action: run gpu-triage collector, tag upload with `alert_id=xb-20260315-001` and `host=gpu-prod-052`.

matt: For parsing/quick attribution we want a small correlator tool that scans a tarball and extracts: Xid lines, ECC correctable/uncorrectable diffs, GPU temperature spikes, driver stack traces, and any kernel oops. I put a tiny Python parser skeleton below (v comfy as a gist):
```python
# parse_xid_ecc.py (very small)
import sys, re
from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET
archive = sys.argv[1]
# assume nvidia-smi -q output is in nvidia-smi.txt
with open('nvidia-smi.txt') as f:
    txt = f.read()
# extract ECC counts (simple regex)
ecc_re = re.compile(r"ECC Error Count\s*: (\d+)")
for m in ecc_re.finditer(txt):
    print('ECC count', m.group(1))
# show Xid lines from dmesg
with open('dmesg.txt') as f:
    for l in f:
        if 'Xid' in l or 'error' in l.lower():
            print(l.strip())
```

sofia: That parser is fine as a starting point. We should normalize ECC delta vs previous snapshot (so we can tell real-time change). Store last N snapshots per host in S3 and compute diffs on upload via a small lambda.

ryan: Ops concerns: the collector must be low-risk. Avoid running any heavy `nvidia-bug-report.sh` in prod automatically. Keep outputs read-only. Also guard AWS creds. We can implement ephemeral IAM roles via instance profile.

ashley: Good call. For automation I propose: detect Xid rate > 2/min -> infra-bot posts alert and runs `gpu-triage --scan --s3-tag alert_id=...` which runs the script in a constrained container, uploads artifact, and posts S3 link to thread. Tagging: host, gpu-uuid, driver-version, kube-node, alert_id.

kyle: FYI, small sample of what we want surfaced first in the S3 object (so triagers don't have to download everything): a single JSON summary file at root of the tarball with fields: ts, host, xids_found: [..], ecc_before, ecc_after, top_temp, driver, gpu_uuid, suspect_pod_list. Keep that tiny.

ashley: I can prototype the systemd unit to run collector on demand and a Lambda to compute diffs. Will drop a draft PR later today.

matt: Awesome. One more quick grep for triage: `dmesg -T | egrep -i "Xid|GPU|NVRM|nvidia" | tail -n 200` — put that at top of the collector summary.

sofia: Also add `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,gpu_uuid,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv` for a quick CSV time-series snapshot.

ashley: Thanks everyone — goal is to cut median time-to-first-attribution for GPU faults by 3x. I'll post the PR link once prototype is up.

infra-bot: Action created: `gpu-triage/collector-prototype` assigned to ashley, matt. ETA: 2d.

kyle: If you want I can add a tiny Grafana panel that shows recent uploads and alert correlation (node -> latest triage ts).

ashley: Please do. That will make on-call life easier. :thumbsup:
